reports.title: Basic medical history – Initial diagnosis Multiple Myeloma

sections.name: Medical history
sections.content: The 64-year-old patient presents after out-of-town evaluation. For 6 months, he has experienced progressive back pain (LWK3 fracture, externally treated), weight loss of 8 kg, and marked fatigue. Pre-existing conditions: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (known since 2012, anticoagulation with Apixaban), mild renal insufficiency CKD IIIa (creatinine 1.4 mg/dl baseline before diagnosis).

sections.name: Pre-existing conditions
sections.content:
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (since 2012) – anticoagulation with Apixaban 5 mg 1-0-1.
Mild renal insufficiency CKD IIIa (baseline creatinine 1.4 mg/dl, eGFR ~52 ml/min).  
Arterial hypertension, Amlodipin 5 mg + Ramipril 5 mg.  
Fatty liver (steatosis hepatis, grade 1, sonographically) – mild hepatic function impairment.

reports.title: Bone marrow biopsy – Initial diagnosis

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Bone marrow core biopsy from 08/09/2016.
Cellularity: approx. 80–90%.
Diffuse infiltration by mature plasma cells, degree of infiltration approx. 70%.
Immunohistochemistry: CD138+, IgA+, lambda-dominant, CD19-, CD56+.
Gomori: MF-1.

sections.name: FISH result
sections.content:
FISH (09/2016):
- del(17p): negative
- t(4;14): POSITIVE (IgH-FGFR3 translocation in 68% of cells) – high-risk cytogenetics
- t(14;16): negative
- 1q21 gain: POSITIVE (55% of cells)
Conclusion: t(4;14) and 1q21 gain as high-risk features.

sections.name: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA light chain lambda.
ISS stage III (β2-microglobulin 8.2 mg/l, albumin 2.9 g/dl).
R-ISS stage III (ISS III + high-risk cytogenetics t(4;14)).
Myeloma kidney failure: creatinine rise to 3.2 mg/dl on admission (light chain nephropathy).

reports.title: Physician letter – Initial diagnosis, emergency initiation of VCD

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Hematological diagnoses:
Multiple myeloma, IgA light chain lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
ISS stage III, R-ISS stage III
High-risk cytogenetics: t(4;14), 1q21 gain
Osseous manifestations: LWK3 compression fracture, disseminated osteolytic lesions BWK8, BWK12, pelvis, left femur

Comorbidities:
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (since 2012)
Renal insufficiency CKD IIIa (acutely worsened to CKD V on admission – myeloma kidney)
Mild hepatic steatosis
Arterial hypertension

sections.name: Therapy plan
sections.content:
Emergency initiation of VCD (bortezomib/cyclophosphamide/dexamethasone) due to myeloma kidney and ISS stage III; 4 cycles planned.
Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m² s.c. days 1, 4, 8, 11 / 21-day cycle.
Cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² p.o. days 1, 8, 15.
Dexamethasone 40 mg days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12.
Zoledronic acid 4 mg i.v. (after renal reconstitution).

sections.name: Renal failure
sections.content: Acute renal failure due to light chain nephropathy (cast nephropathy) on admission 08/09/2016. Creatinine on admission: 3.2 mg/dl (baseline 1.4 mg/dl). eGFR: 18 ml/min. Dialysis required due to hyperkalaemia (potassium 6.2 mmol/l) and fluid overload: haemodialysis commenced 09/09/2016, 3 sessions until partial recovery. After 3 weeks VCD: creatinine 1.8 mg/dl, dialysis discontinued. External renal biopsy: cast nephropathy confirmed.

sections.name: ECOG
sections.content: ECOG performance status: 2 (reduced general condition, bedridden <50% of the day, impaired activities of daily living).

reports.title: Skeletal CT – Staging

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Whole-body low-dose CT from 12/09/2016.
Spine: LWK3 compression fracture (approx. 40% height loss). Lytic lesions at BWK8 (12 mm), BWK12 (8 mm), LWK1 (10 mm).
Pelvis: Extensive osteolytic lesions bilateral os ilium, left os ischii (largest lesion 25 mm).
Long bones: Lytic lesion left femur, proximal (14 mm).
Skull: Diffuse osteopenia, scattered small calvarial lesions (<5 mm).
Conclusion: Disseminated osseous involvement in multiple myeloma with LWK3 compression fracture. Fracture risk at left femur.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – Initial diagnosis MM IgA lambda, treatment planning

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Initial diagnosis of multiple myeloma IgA lambda in a 64-year-old patient with acute renal failure (myeloma kidney) and high-risk cytogenetics.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: MM IgA lambda, ISS III, R-ISS III. t(4;14) and 1q21 gain. LWK3 fracture, disseminated osteolytic lesions. Acute renal failure (creatinine 3.2 mg/dl) requiring dialysis (from 09/09/2016). ECOG 2.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content: Emergency VCD induction therapy (bortezomib/cyclophosphamide/dexamethasone) for myeloma kidney – no IMiD-based regimen due to renal failure. Goal: rapid response, renal recovery, then autologous SCT if kidney recovered and ECOG ≤2. Orthopedic consult for fracture risk at left femur. Zoledronic acid after renal reconstitution (creatinine <3.0 mg/dl).

reports.title: Physician letter – VCD cycle 1 completion, dialysis weaning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After VCD cycle 1: creatinine decline – dialysis weaning

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
VCD cycle 1 (started 15/09/2016, 21-day cycle) completed. Third haemodialysis session on 15/09/2016.
Creatinine under therapy: 3.2 mg/dl → 2.4 mg/dl (28/09/2016) → 1.9 mg/dl (10/10/2016). Dialysis no longer required since 04/10/2016.
IgA 42.0 g/l (baseline 58.2 g/l, -28%). Declining trend.
Calcium normalised (2.4 mmol/l).
Hb 9.4 g/dl, transfusion 2 packed red blood cells (01/10/2016).
Potassium within normal range.

sections.name: Chronic medication
sections.content:
Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m² s.c. days 1, 4, 8, 11 (cycle 2 from 06/10/2016)
Cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² p.o. days 1, 8, 15
Dexamethasone 40 mg days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12
Valacyclovir 500 mg 1-0-1 (herpes prophylaxis)
Pantoprazole 40 mg 1-0-0
Apixaban paused (dialysis, bleeding risk – cardiology consulted)
Amlodipine 5 mg 1-0-0

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Start VCD cycle 2 on 06/10/2016. Weekly renal function and lab monitoring. Zoledronic acid as soon as creatinine <2.0 mg/dl stably.

reports.title: Physician's letter – VCD Cycle 2 Follow-up

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After VCD cycle 2: partial renal recovery, first signs of remission

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
VCD cycle 2 (06/10–26/10/2016) completed. Outpatient therapy.
Creatinine 1.8 mg/dl (eGFR 38 ml/min), stable. No dialysis required.
IgA 32.5 g/l (-44% vs. baseline 58.2 g/l).
FLC lambda 1240 mg/l (baseline 1840 mg/l, -33%).
Hb 10.2 g/dl. No transfusion-requiring anaemia currently.
Zoledronic acid 4 mg i.v. first dose on 28/10/2016 (creatinine <2.0 mg/dl).
Neuropathy: fingertip tingling bilateral grade 1 under bortezomib. No dose reduction.

sections.name: Maintenance medication
sections.content: VCD as before, cycle 3 from 27/10/2016. Zoledronic acid 4 mg i.v. monthly. Apixaban 2.5 mg 1-0-1 (reduced dose, renal insufficiency CKD IIIb).

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Cycle 3 follow-up mid-November. Remission assessment after cycle 4.

reports.title: Whole‑body low‑dose CT – follow‑up under VCD

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgA lambda, after 2 cycles VCD, follow-up of osteolytic lesions.

Clinical question: Progression of osseous lesions? New fracture risk?

Prior imaging: WB-LDCT 12/09/2016.

Findings: Spine: LWK3 compression fracture stable (no further height loss). BWK8, BWK12, LWK1 lytic lesions stable. No new vertebral fractures. Pelvis: Osteolytic lesions bilateral os ilium stable. Femur: Lytic lesion proximal left 14 mm stable. No new critical fracture risk.

Conclusion: Stable osseous situation under ongoing VCD therapy. No progression of osteolytic lesions. No new fracture detected. Bisphosphonate therapy recommended (already being initiated).

reports.title: Physician's letter – VCD Cycle 3 Follow-up

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After VCD cycle 3: sustained remission, ECOG improvement

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
Cycle 3 VCD (27/10–16/11/2016) completed. Outpatient.
IgA 22.8 g/l (-61% vs. baseline). FLC lambda 820 mg/l (-55%). Patient ECOG: 1 (significant improvement, mobile, daily activities possible again).
Creatinine 1.7 mg/dl (eGFR 40 ml/min), stable. Hb 10.8 g/dl.
Neuropathy grade 1 stable.
Radiological follow-up 20/11/2016: stable situation, no fracture.

sections.name: Maintenance medication
sections.content: VCD cycle 4 started 17/11/2016. Zoledronic acid dose 2. Valacyclovir, pantoprazole, apixaban, amlodipine as before.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Remission assessment after cycle 4 (approx. 02/2017). Stem cell mobilization planned if adequate response.

reports.title: Physician letter – Response after 4 cycles VCD, ASCT preparation

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After 4 cycles VCD: PR
Recovered from acute renal failure (dialysis 09/2016, now CKD IIIb)
Planning autologous stem cell transplantation

sections.name: Therapeutic response
sections.content:
After 4 cycles VCD:
- IgA: 18.4 g/l (baseline 58 g/l)
- Serum immunofixation: positive
- Free light chains lambda: 420 mg/l (baseline 1840 mg/l)
Assessment: PR (partial response)

Renal function after VCD: creatinine 1.8 mg/dl (eGFR 38 ml/min), significant improvement vs. admission (creatinine 3.2 mg/dl). Dialysis no longer required since 10/2016.

Cumulative bortezomib dose to date: 4 cycles × 4 doses × 1.3 mg/m² × 1.88 m² BSA = approx. 38.9 mg total.
No doxorubicin exposure.

sections.name: Stem cell mobilization
sections.content: Stem cell mobilization with G‑CSF successful. CD34+: 5,8 × 10^6 cells/kg (1 transplantation possible).

sections.name: Planning
sections.content:
HD-melphalan (200 mg/m²) + autologous SCT planned for 03/2017.
Cumulative melphalan dose (planned): 200 mg/m² × 1.88 m² BSA = 376 mg total.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – PR after VCD × 4, ASCT planned

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: Response assessment after 4 cycles VCD in MM IgA lambda, ISS III. Planning ASCT.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: PR (IgA 18.4 g/l, -68%). Renal function recovered (creatinine 1.8 mg/dl, dialysis discontinued). ECOG 2→1. Stem cell mobilization performed (CD34+: 5.8 × 10^6/kg). High-risk cytogenetics t(4;14) persists.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content: HD-melphalan 200 mg/m² + autologous SCT in March 2017. Target melphalan dose: 376 mg (BSA 1.88 m²). Post-ASCT lenalidomide maintenance considering renal insufficiency (reduced dose if necessary). Next tumor board after ASCT discharge.

reports.title: Physician letter – Admission for ASCT, HD‑melphalan conditioning

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After VCD × 4: PR
Admission for autologous stem cell transplantation

sections.name: Admission and Conditioning
sections.content:
Inpatient admission on 06/03/2017. Admission labs 06/03/2017: Hb 10.8 g/dl, leukocytes 5.2 G/l, neutrophils 3.1 G/l, platelets 142 G/l. Creatinine 1.9 mg/dl, eGFR 37 ml/min (CKD IIIb).
Conditioning: HD-melphalan 200 mg/m² (176 mg, reduced to 176 mg due to GFR <40 ml/min – renal insufficiency. Total dose 376 mg minus renal adjustment: 344 mg) i.v. on 08/03/2017 (D-2). Hyperhydration 3 l/m²/d.
Stem cell reinfusion: 10/03/2017 (D0), 5.8 × 10^6 CD34+/kg. Uneventful.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: G-CSF from D+5. Daily blood count and vital sign monitoring. Isolation until engraftment.

reports.title: Physician letter – ASCT discharge after engraftment

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After HD-melphalan + ASCT (10/03/2017): engraftment day +13
Discharge day +24

sections.name: Inpatient course
sections.content:
Engraftment: neutrophils >0.5 G/l on day +13 (23/03/2017). Mucositis grade 2 (day +5 to +12, opioid patch analgesia). No transfusion-requiring anaemia after day +7 (Hb nadir 8.2 g/dl day +8, 2 packed red blood cells transfused).
Post-engraftment infection-free. Platelets >50 G/l on day +17, >100 G/l on day +22.
Discharge labs 03/04/2017: Hb 10.6 g/dl, leukocytes 5.4 G/l, neutrophils 3.8 G/l, platelets 104 G/l (rising). Creatinine 2.0 mg/dl (stable CKD IIIb).
IgA 12.4 g/l (preliminary response assessment after ASCT).

sections.name: Chronic medication
sections.content:
Valacyclovir 500 mg 1-0-1
Pantoprazole 40 mg 1-0-0
Fluconazole 100 mg/d (until 6 weeks post-ASCT)
Apixaban 2.5 mg 1-0-1 (atrial fibrillation)
Amlodipine 5 mg 1-0-0
Ramipril 2.5 mg (dose halved, CKD)

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Outpatient follow-up day +45 on 24/04/2017. Formal remission assessment after 3 months (06/2017).

reports.title: Physician letter – Post‑ASCT outpatient control day +45

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After HD-melphalan + ASCT: day +45

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
Patient [correction: male] in stable condition. Fatigue declining, ECOG 1. No fever, no infection. Mucositis fully resolved.
Labs 22/04/2017: Hb 11.4 g/dl, leukocytes 6.2 G/l, neutrophils 4.0 G/l, platelets 186 G/l. Creatinine 1.9 mg/dl, eGFR 40 ml/min. IgA 10.2 g/l, FLC lambda 142 mg/l.
Atrial fibrillation: paroxysmal, no rate increase. ECG: sinus rhythm.

sections.name: Chronic medication
sections.content: As at discharge. Fluconazole stopped (>6 weeks post-ASCT).

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Formal remission assessment (IgA, FLC, immunofixation, bone marrow biopsy) after 3 months (June 2017). Discussion of lenalidomide maintenance considering renal function.

reports.title: Physician letter – post‑ASCT control

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After HD-melphalan (200 mg/m²) + ASCT (03/2017): VGPR
Kidney: CKD IIIb stable

sections.name: Course after ASCT
sections.content:
Autologous stem cell transplantation with HD-melphalan on 10/03/2017. Engraftment day +14. Uncomplicated course, no significant mucositis. Discharge day +20.

Remission assessment 06/2017:
- IgA: 6.2 g/l (baseline 58 g/l)
- Serum immunofixation: positive (weakly)
- Free light chains lambda: 62 mg/l
Assessment: VGPR

reports.title: Physician letter – post‑ASCT 6‑month control, VGPR confirmed

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After VCD × 4 + HD-melphalan + ASCT (03/2017): VGPR
Lenalidomide maintenance feasible with restrictions (CKD IIIb)

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
6-month follow-up post-ASCT. Remission stable. General condition: ECOG 1, significant improvement vs. initial diagnosis.
Labs 15/09/2017: IgA 6.2 g/l, immunofixation: positive (weakly). FLC lambda 62 mg/l. Hb 12.2 g/dl, leukocytes 5.8 G/l, neutrophils 3.4 G/l. Creatinine 1.8 mg/dl (eGFR 41 ml/min).
Assessment: VGPR sustained.
Lenalidomide maintenance: started lenalidomide 10 mg/d (reduced due to CKD IIIb, standard dose 25 mg contraindicated). Started 01/09/2017.

sections.name: Chronic medication
sections.content:
Lenalidomide 10 mg/d days 1–21, 28-day cycle (renal insufficiency-adjusted)
Valacyclovir 500 mg 1-0-1
Pantoprazole 40 mg 1-0-0
Apixaban 2.5 mg 1-0-1
Amlodipine 5 mg 1-0-0
Ramipril 2.5 mg 1-0-0
Aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0 (thrombosis prophylaxis under lenalidomide)

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Next follow-up 12/2017. Monthly blood count monitoring by GP.

reports.title: Physician letter – post‑ASCT 9‑month control, lenalidomide maintenance

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
VGPR under lenalidomide maintenance
CKD IIIb stable

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
Patient in good general condition, ECOG 1. Lenalidomide 10 mg well tolerated for 3 months. Mild fatigue grade 1, no diarrhoea, no infection.
Labs 08/12/2017: IgA 6.8 g/l (slightly rising, but still in VGPR range), immunofixation positive. FLC lambda 74 mg/l. Hb 11.8 g/dl, neutrophils 2.4 G/l, platelets 158 G/l. Creatinine 1.8 mg/dl.
Assessment: VGPR sustained. Slight IgA rise, not yet progression.

sections.name: Long‑term medication
sections.content: As before. Zoledronic acid dose 7 (monthly).

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Closer monitoring in view of slight IgA rise. Next follow-up 03/2018 with comprehensive labs including FLC and immunofixation. Annual skeletal CT follow-up 03/2018.

reports.title: Skeletal CT – Annual follow‑up

sections.name: Full report
sections.content:
Clinical information: MM IgA lambda, after ASCT 03/2017 and VCD induction, 12-month follow-up under lenalidomide maintenance.

Clinical question: New osteolytic lesions? Fracture progression?

Prior imaging: WB-LDCT 20/11/2016.

Findings: Spine: LWK3 compression fracture with unchanged height loss. No new fracture. No new osteolytic lesion at BWK8, BWK12, LWK1 (stable). No new vertebral bodies involved. Pelvis: Os ilium osteolytic lesions stable. Left femur: Lytic lesion proximal stable (14 mm). Skull: Known small calvarial lesions, no progression.

Conclusion: Stable osseous situation without evidence of new osteolytic lesions or fracture events. Consistent with sustained remission under lenalidomide maintenance.

reports.title: Physician letter – Post‑ASCT 14‑month follow‑up, IgA increase

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
VGPR under lenalidomide maintenance, current IgA rise – monitoring

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
Labs 11/05/2018: IgA 14.8 g/l (rise vs. 6.8 g/l 12/2017), immunofixation positive. FLC lambda 182 mg/l (rising). Hb 11.2 g/dl, creatinine 1.9 mg/dl.
Assessment: IgA rise >25% vs. nadir – formally partial progression (no CRAB criteria met yet). No clinical evidence of new organ damage. Imaging 03/2018 stable.
Monitoring changed to monthly. Tumor board presentation planned.

sections.name: Long‑term medication
sections.content: Lenalidomide maintenance continued at 10 mg/d. Other medications unchanged.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Tumor board presentation 20/05/2018. Next laboratory monitoring monthly. Skeletal CT if clinically indicated.

reports.title: Bone marrow biopsy – first relapse

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Bone marrow core biopsy from 25/07/2018.
Cellularity: 75%.
Detection of a plasma cell infiltrate: approx. 30% of nucleated cells.
Immunohistochemistry: CD138+, lambda+, IgA+, CD19-, CD56+ (as at initial diagnosis).

sections.name: FISH result
sections.content:
FISH (07/2018):
- t(4;14): POSITIVE (persists, 65% of cells)
- 1q21 gain: POSITIVE (persists, 58% of cells)
- del(17p): negative
Comparison with initial diagnosis: t(4;14) and 1q21 gain unchanged persistent.

sections.name: Diagnosis
sections.content: Histologically and cytogenetically confirmed first relapse of multiple myeloma after ASCT. Plasma cell infiltration 30% (baseline initial diagnosis 70%). No new high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – progression under Lenalidomid, relapse therapy

sections.name: Reason for discussion
sections.content: IgA rise and development of new osteolytic lesions on CT (20/07/2018) under lenalidomide maintenance after ASCT in MM IgA lambda, ISS III, t(4;14).

sections.name: Findings
sections.content: IgA 24.5 g/l (post-ASCT nadir 6.2 g/l), new osteolytic lesions CT 20/07/2018. Lenalidomide-refractory. BM biopsy 25/07/2018: 30% plasma cell infiltrate, t(4;14) persists.

sections.name: Decision
sections.content: Start 2nd line therapy with carfilzomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (KRd) from 01/08/2018. Caution: history of atrial fibrillation – carfilzomib with cardiac vigilance; pre-treatment echocardiography, cardiologist involved. Next tumor board after 4 cycles.

reports.title: Cardiology consult – echocardiography before Carfilzomib

sections.name: Question
sections.content: Cardiac baseline assessment for planned carfilzomib therapy. Known paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (apixaban). Exclusion of relevant left ventricular dysfunction.

sections.name: Finding
sections.content:
Transthoracic echocardiography 06/08/2018:
LV function: Normal, EF 55% (biplane).
No wall motion abnormalities.
Aortic valve: Mild aortic sclerosis without haemodynamic significance.
Mitral valve: Mild mitral regurgitation (grade 1).
No pericardial effusion. Right heart unremarkable.

sections.name: Assessment
sections.content: Adequate systolic LV function for carfilzomib therapy. Cardiological co-management under carfilzomib recommended. Repeat echo after 3 cycles.

reports.title: Physician letter – KRd cycles 2–3, cardiotoxicity signal

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
1st relapse, 2nd line KRd
Under carfilzomib: fluid retention grade 2, echocardiography deterioration

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
KRd cycles 1–2 (01/08–28/08/2018) uncomplicated. Cycle 3 (29/08–18/09/2018): increasing leg oedema (grade 2), exertional dyspnoea. Echocardiography 01/10/2018: EF 50% (baseline 55%). No pericardial effusion.
Response labs: IgA 18.2 g/l (baseline 24.5 g/l, -26%). PR threshold not yet reached (-50%). FLC lambda 420 mg/l.
Cardiological recommendation: carfilzomib dose reduction to 20 mg/m² (from 27 mg/m²) in cycle 4.
Atrial fibrillation: stable, no rate increase.

sections.name: Chronic medication
sections.content:
Carfilzomib 20 mg/m² (reduced) days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16 / 28-day cycle
Lenalidomide 25 mg days 1–21
Dexamethasone 40 mg weekly
Furosemide 40 mg/d p.o. (oedema therapy)
Apixaban 2.5 mg 1-0-1
Amlodipine, ramipril, valacyclovir as before

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Cardiological follow-up (echo) after cycle 4. Lenalidomide dose remains 25 mg (no current renal problem under KRd). Next oncological follow-up end of November.

reports.title: Cardiology consult – echo follow‑up under Carfilzomib cycle 6

sections.name: Question
sections.content: Cardiovascular follow-up under carfilzomib in known atrial fibrillation and grade 2 fluid retention.

sections.name: Findings
sections.content:
Echocardiography 10/12/2018:
LV EF: 48% (decrease from 55% pre-therapy to 48%).
New: Mild inferolateral hypokinesia. No pericardial effusion. Diastolic dysfunction grade 1.
Leg oedema reduced under furosemide.

sections.name: Assessment
sections.content: Mild carfilzomib-associated cardiotoxicity (EF reduction of 7%, to 48%). No clinical signs of heart failure. Recommendation: carfilzomib discontinuation after current cycle (6 cycles planned, now completed). No further carfilzomib exposure. Continue cardiological co-management and echo monitoring every 6 months.

reports.title: Physician letter – KRd cycle 6 completed, response evaluation

sections.name: Diagnoses
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
After KRd × 6: SD (stable disease), end of therapy
Carfilzomib-associated cardiotoxicity (EF 48%)

sections.name: Current course
sections.content:
KRd 6 cycles (08/2018–12/2018) completed. Final assessment:
- IgA: 22.1 g/l (baseline 24.5 g/l – only marginal reduction)
- FLC lambda: 380 mg/l (baseline 680 mg/l – 44% reduction, but IgA as primary marker insufficient)
- Immunofixation: positive
- Formal response: SD (no ≥50% reduction of M-protein)

Cardiology 10/12/2018: EF 48% (from 55%). Carfilzomib discontinued after 6 cycles due to cardiotoxicity and lack of response.
Refractory status now: lenalidomide-refractory, carfilzomib-refractory.

sections.name: Further procedure
sections.content: Tumor board 20/01/2019. Next therapy line for high-risk refractory MM: discuss PACE regimen (or other salvage therapy).

reports.title: Physician letter – First relapse, start of KRd.

sections.name: Diagnoses.
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma, IgA LC lambda (initial diagnosis 09/2016)
1st relapse (07/2018) after VCD + ASCT
Start 2nd line: carfilzomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (KRd)

sections.name: Relapse.
sections.content:
During follow-up 07/2018, IgA rise to 24.5 g/l. New osteolytic lesions on skeletal CT 20/07/2018: new osteolytic lesions at BWK5 (12 mm) and os sacrum (10 mm). First documented new osteolytic lesions on CT: 20/07/2018.
Bone marrow biopsy 25/07/2018: plasma cell infiltration 30%, t(4;14) positive, 1q21 gain persistent.

sections.name: Therapy plan 2nd line.
sections.content:
Start carfilzomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (KRd) from 01/08/2018.
Carfilzomib 20 mg/m² days 1/2 cycle 1, then 27 mg/m² days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16 / 28-day cycle.
Lenalidomide 25 mg/d p.o. days 1–21.
Dexamethasone 40 mg weekly.

Note: Carfilzomib used with heightened cardiac caution due to history of atrial fibrillation. Pre-treatment echocardiography: EF 55%, no pericardial effusion.

sections.name: Carfilzomib tolerability.
sections.content:
Under KRd after 2 cycles: grade 2 dyspnoea and new fluid retention (leg oedema). Suspected carfilzomib-associated cardiac toxicity. Echocardiography cycle 3: EF 48% (decrease from 55% to 48%). Carfilzomib dose reduction to 20 mg/m², continued monitoring. Regular cardiological co-management. No pericardial effusion, no heart failure. Atrial fibrillation not worsened.

Carfilzomib period: 01/08/2018 – 31/12/2018 (5 months, total 6 cycles).

reports.title: Physician letter – Response under KRd, therapy termination.

sections.name: Response KRd.
sections.content:
After 6 cycles KRd:
- IgA: 22.1 g/l (baseline 24.5 g/l, only slight reduction)
- Serum immunofixation: positive
- Free light chains lambda: 380 mg/l
Assessment: SD (stable disease) – insufficient tumour mass reduction.
KRd therapy discontinued due to lack of response and carfilzomib toxicity.

Post-KRd refractory: lenalidomide-refractory (no reduction under KRd), carfilzomib-refractory (no reduction, toxicity).

sections.name: Further procedure.
sections.content: Discussion at tumor board. Next line: PACE regimen (cisplatin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, etoposide) for refractory disease.

reports.title: Tumor board decision – SD after KRd, 3rd line PACE.

sections.name: Reason for discussion.
sections.content: Treatment planning after SD under KRd × 6 in triple-refractory MM IgA lambda (PI-refractory [carfilzomib], IMiD-refractory [len], alkylators not yet used as rescue).

sections.name: Refractoriness status.

sections.name: 3rd‑line therapy

Doxorubicin period: within PACE: 01/04/2019 – 04/04/2019 (cycle 1), 22/04/2019 – 25/04/2019 (cycle 2). Cumulative doxorubicin dose: 2 cycles × 4 days × 10 mg/m² × 1.88 m² BSA = approx. 150 mg total.

After 2 cycles PACE, therapy discontinued due to toxicity.
